query_preparation.promotion_rule: Official register/search/calculator/statistical capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains PENDING_RAW_RESPONSE until candidate-specific address/site/permission/deed/ward evidence and provenance are captured.

batches.c: VOA rateable value is property-specific taxation evidence. Exact address/valuation-list entry is required; it is not the business-rates bill or market rent.
The 2026 non-domestic revaluation took effect on 1 April 2026. Candidate evidence must use the current list and preserve effective date.
The VOA service can show similar properties, but comparables do not become the candidate property's rateable value without exact matching.
Council Tax bands are address-specific domestic taxation records. Exact address lookup is required before association with a candidate.

batches.t: Council Tax band versus market-value guard
batches.c: A Council Tax band is not a current market valuation and must not be converted directly into development value or sale price.
VOA maintains separate domestic Council Tax and non-domestic rating lists. Proposed use/current hereditament status must be resolved before using either record.
The Appeals Casework Portal supports case searches. Exact site address, LPA reference or appeal reference is required before linking an appeal to a candidate.
The published casework database covers a rolling five-year selection of decisions. Missing records outside scope are not evidence of no appeal history.
Planning Inspectorate guidance notes some appeal categorisation is subjective; source fields and case type must be preserved.

batches.t: Appeal decision versus current permission gate
batches.c: An appeal decision is case-specific and time-specific. Later permissions, variations or legal challenges must be resolved before treating it as current site status.
Most recent decision letters can be searched through the portal; older material may require the LPA. Incomplete online history is not a negative result.
Historic allowed/dismissed appeals cannot be converted into a parcel permission probability without proposal-specific planning analysis.
January-March 2026 is the latest published quarterly planning-application statistical release found in this wave. Authority-level activity is context, not site outcome.
Planning performance speed measures the share decided within statutory/agreed periods. It is an authority service metric, not a guaranteed candidate determination time.
Decision quality is measured partly through decisions overturned at appeal. This is authority-level performance and not permission probability for a candidate.
The Planning Performance Dashboard year ending March 2026 supports current authority benchmarking; exact Enfield/Havering/Lambeth rows must be resolved before comparison.
The April-June 2026 release is provisionally scheduled for September 2026. It must not be fabricated or treated as currently published data.
Higher-risk building controls apply at the statutory height/storey threshold with qualifying residential/hospital/care-home use. Exact scheme height/storeys/use are required.
For qualifying higher-risk building work, Building Safety Regulator approval is required before starting. A candidate coordinate alone cannot establish Gateway-2 applicability.
BSR transparency data through June 2026 provide system performance context, not a candidate approval forecast.
London's share of BSR cases is regional workload context only and must not become a site-specific delay or approval probability.
The Building Safety Levy starts 1 October 2026. It is a future cost rule on 25 July 2026 and must not be applied early.
Levy rates vary by local authority and previously developed land status. Exact authority, chargeable floorspace and land-status inputs are required.
The levy depends on application timing and exemptions. Applications submitted before 1 October 2026 have different treatment; candidate cost remains unscored without scheme facts.
Enfield CIL generally applies to qualifying new floorspace/new dwellings. Exact proposed use, floorspace, permission date and relief status are required.
The 2026 annual CIL summary and charging zones are listed by the council. Exact candidate zone/use and indexed rate are required before cost calculation.
Local CIL is additional to Mayoral CIL where applicable. Both liabilities must be assessed separately and combined only for an exact scheme.
The council states residential contributions are generally sought at ten or more units and commercial at more than 1,000 square metres, with case-specific exceptions. Exact scheme scale is required.
The online register contains applications, decision notices, conditions and appeals. Exact address/reference and current decision status are required.
CIL notices and S106 trigger/discharge status are permission-specific. A historic agreement or liability notice does not prove an outstanding current obligation.
Havering local CIL has applied to qualifying permissions from 1 September 2019. Exact permission date, use, floorspace and relief status are required.
Havering local CIL can apply in addition to Mayoral CIL. Candidate liability cannot be inferred from borough location alone.
Havering states every S106 agreement is attached to a specific planning permission. Exact planning reference/site match is mandatory.
The council's planning process and register support proposal-specific due diligence. Pre-application advice is not planning permission.
CIL payment and S106 discharge require site/permission-specific confirmation. Missing public confirmation is not proof that no liability remains.
Lambeth's 2022 CIL schedule applies according to the date development is first permitted. Exact permission/effectivity date is required.
Lambeth publishes a 2026 annual CIL rate summary. Exact use, zone, indexed rate and chargeable floorspace are required.
The council states approved development can be liable at 100 square metres or more of new floorspace or one or more dwellings. Relief/exemption and exact proposal facts remain required.
The council's calculator is indicative and explicitly not the final binding liability. Liability/Demand Notices control the payable amount.
S106 obligations must be necessary, directly related, and fairly/reasonably related in scale and kind. Exact proposal and deed are required.
S106 deed copies and compliance confirmations are reference-specific. Exact deed/application number is required before declaring obligations satisfied or outstanding.
Enfield's new selective licensing scheme is approved but starts 1 September 2026. On 25 July 2026 it is a future rule and cannot be applied as already effective.
Enfield's additional HMO licensing scheme has operated borough-wide since 1 September 2025 for qualifying shared homes. Exact occupancy/use and address are required.
Havering's new schemes took effect 18 March 2026: selective licensing is ward-limited while additional HMO licensing is borough-wide. Exact ward/address and occupancy model are required.
Lambeth selective licensing phases cover 23 of 25 wards, excluding Vauxhall and Waterloo & South Bank. Exact candidate ward/address and tenancy model are required.
Lambeth HMO licensing and planning permission are separate regimes; Article 4 can change planning requirements. Exact occupancy, ward, use class and licensing record are required.
